Missouri property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment.

What the official sources say

  • An appeal must be filed with the county Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. (Paying Property Taxes Under Protest And/Or Appeal Options | State Tax Commission; source)
  • A Complaint for Review of Assessment must be filed with the State Tax Commission by September 30 of the year of assessment or within 30 days of the Board of Equalization decision, whichever is later. (File An Appeal | Missouri State Tax Commission; source)
  • Property taxes are due no later than December 31; the owner may appeal even if taxes are unpaid, or pay the full bill by December 31 marked 'paid under protest'. (Paying Property Taxes Under Protest And/Or Appeal Options | State Tax Commission; source)
  • Real property is assessed at percentages of true value: 19% for subclass (1) (residential), 12% for subclass (2) (agricultural), 32% for subclass (3) (commercial). (RSMo 137.115; source)
  • In a first class charter county or a city not within a county, at an STC or court appeal the assessor may not advocate a valuation higher than the value finally determined by the assessor or the board of equalization, whichever is higher. (RSMo 138.060; source)
  • Delinquent tax sales are held on the fourth Monday in August of each year. (RSMo 140.150; source)
  • The owner, lienholder, occupant or other interested person may redeem within one year of the sale by paying the purchase price, costs, interest per the certificate (not above 10% annually), and later taxes paid with 8% interest; the right to redeem is defeasible until the purchaser acquires the deed. (RSMo 140.340; source)

Missouri offers property tax relief for qualifying homeowners, and official sources explain the rules.

What the official sources say

  • The Missouri Property Tax Credit Claim ('circuit breaker') gives credit to certain senior citizens and 100 percent disabled individuals for a portion of real estate taxes or rent paid. (Property Tax Credit | Missouri Department of Revenue; source)
  • The credit is a maximum of $750 for renters and $1,100 for owners who owned and occupied their home, based on taxes or rent paid and total household income. (Property Tax Credit | Missouri Department of Revenue; source)
  • A county authorized to impose a property tax may grant a homestead property tax credit to eligible owners age 62 or older (owner of record of a homestead). (RSMo 137.1050; source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Missouri evictions follow notice and court steps set by state law.

What the official sources say

  • Rent and possession: after demand for unpaid rent, the landlord may file a verified statement with an associate circuit judge; the clerk issues a summons to the tenant and occupants to show cause why possession should not be restored. (RSMo 535.020; source)
  • The one-month termination notice under 441.060 is not required before filing a rent-and-possession statement. (RSMo 535.020; source)
  • A tenancy at will or for less than one year may be terminated by one month's written notice; a month-to-month tenancy ends on a rent-paying date not less than one month after receipt of written notice. (RSMo 441.060; source)
  • If the officer fails to deliver possession within seven days of delivery of the writ, the landlord may within 60 days of judgment, with law enforcement present and without breach of the peace, change locks and remove property. (RSMo 441.060; source)
  • After a foreclosure sale, the new owner must give a residential-tenant occupant notice that the sale occurred and that the occupant has not less than ten business days to vacate; no unlawful detainer action may begin within ten business days of the notice. (RSMo 534.030; source)
  • Section 534.030 states that nothing in it creates a tenancy between the new owner and the occupant. (RSMo 534.030; source)

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

This guide covers what official sources say about Missouri transfer on death deeds.

What the official sources say

  • A deed conveying real property to a designated grantee beneficiary that expressly states it is not to take effect until the owner's death transfers the interest on death if executed and recorded with the recorder of deeds before the owner's death. (RSMo 461.025; source)
  • A beneficiary deed need not be supported by consideration or delivered to the grantee beneficiary, and may transfer to a trust regardless of revocability. (RSMo 461.025; source)
  • A beneficiary deed not recorded until after the owner's death is not invalidated if otherwise effective by law. (RSMo 461.025; source)
  • Small estate: distributees may take personal and real property without letters if the estate, less liens, debt and encumbrances, does not exceed $40,000, 30 days have passed since death and no letters application is pending. (RSMo 473.097; source)
  • Small estate affidavit is filed with the probate division clerk; a bond is required unless the court dispenses with it, and the filing fee under 483.580 is paid. (RSMo 473.097; source)
  • Distributees may establish their right to succeed to real estate by recording a copy of the affidavit and clerk's certificate with the recorder of deeds in each county where the real property sits. (RSMo 473.097; source)
